title: Hybrid Prometheus bridge and zero-alloc trace batcher for reduced observability overhead
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Background:
Our runtime emits both high-cardinality metrics from internal subsystems and high-throughput traces. The current push-based metrics pipeline and naïve trace forwarder cause noticeable allocation pressure and tail latencies in high-concurrency worker processes. This increases 99th percentile request latency and contributes to noisy autoscaling signals for Dedicated clusters and Private deployments.

Goal:
Introduce a hybrid Prometheus bridge (pull-first with push fallback) and a zero-allocation, preallocated trace batcher + sharded forwarder to reduce per-request allocs, lower tail latencies, and stabilize metric tails under load. Target improvement: 30-50% reduction in observability-related allocations and 20-40% lower 99th percentile latency in the runtime under representative load.

Scope & Non-goals:
- Scope: runtime-side changes (metrics exporter, trace batching/sharding, sampling hooks) and a small adapter in the observability pipeline to accept pull metrics or batched trace blobs. Documentation, rollout flags, and QA harnesses included.
- Non-goal: replacing upstream telemetry backends (Prometheus/OTel collector). This ticket provides an adapter/bridge so upstream remains unchanged.

Design overview:
1) Hybrid Prometheus bridge:
   - Runtime exposes a lightweight /metrics-pull endpoint for low-cardinality, aggregated metrics. The runtime will maintain an in-memory registry with low-allocation scrapes (pre-formatted byte buffers).
   - For high-cardinality or high-frequency counters (per-request labels), runtime will buffer and ship to a local push relay only when traffic patterns indicate pull is insufficient (adaptive overflow).
   - Benefits: typical scrapes become zero-alloc and avoid serialized push churn; push fallback handles bursts without dropping high-cardinality signals.

2) Zero-alloc trace batcher + sharded forwarder:
   - Introduce a preallocated ring buffer per worker group and a single-ownership batcher that serializes spans into pre-sized buffers to avoid per-span heap allocations.
   - Batches are flushed on size/time thresholds and routed to sharded forwarders (one per NUMA/cpu-group) to reduce contention.
   - Add a light-weight sampling hook driven by route/tenant tiers to avoid sending unnecessary spans for low-priority workloads. Sampling decisions are cached in the batcher to avoid repeated lookups.

3) Compatibility shim:
   - A small sidecar adapter (observability bridge) in the collector layer accepts both pull scrapes and push blobs and normalizes them for the existing OTLP pipeline.

Trade-offs considered:
- Complexity: sharded forwarders and preallocated buffers add complexity to the runtime but are isolated behind a metrics/tracing abstraction. We considered a simpler alloc-minimization approach (reuse objects) but expected contention still to hurt tail latencies.
- Signal fidelity: adaptive sampling reduces trace volume which may impact debugging. Mitigation: release sampling knobs (percent, tenant overrides) and keep a small always-on sample.

Implementation plan (approx timeline):
- Week 1: Prototype zero-alloc scrape path and preformatted metric buffer; smoke tests. (Miguel)
- Week 2: Implement ring buffer batcher and basic flush logic; unit tests. (Miguel + Jordan Lee)
- Week 3: Add sharded forwarder and adaptive sampling hook; integration tests with local collector shim. (Team)
- Week 4: End-to-end load tests using the perf-harness dashboard, refine thresholds, add rollout flags. (Asha)
- Week 5: Canary rollout to dev clusters, monitor observability SLOs, iterate on sampling and fallback heuristics. (All)

Testing & metrics:
- Primary metrics: allocations/process, runtime 99th latency, scrape latency, trace throughput, dropped spans, memory RSS.
- Use perf-harness job 'obs-2025/hybrid-bridge' to run 2h soak with realistic LLM token generation workload. Dashboard: https://grafana.internal/redwood/d/hybrid-bridge
- E2E: verify OTLP pipeline acceptance and Prometheus compatibility via the collector shim.

Rollout plan & safety:
- Feature gated behind runtime flag `obs.hybrid_bridge_enabled` (default false).
- Start with canary on internal dev clusters for 48h, then progressively roll to Dedicated non-production pools, then to low-traffic production namespaces.
- Automatic rollback if metric regressions exceed thresholds (allocs +10% or 99th latency +5% relative to baseline).

Open questions & follow-ups:
- Best default thresholds for batch size/time flush for different instance sizes. We'll run autoscaling matrix tests to pick defaults.
- Long-term: evaluate moving sampling decisions upstream in the routing plane to avoid sending spans to runtime at all for some customers.

Links & artifacts:
- Design doc (Confluence): https://confluence.internal/redwood/obs/hybrid-prom-bridge
- Perf harness job: https://ci.internal/redwood/jobs/obs-hybrid-bridge
- Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4412 (WIP)
